clue.text: If returned without hesitation a Conservative finds this simple

definitions.note: a simple is an old word for a medicinal herb

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the turned word goes round the hesitation
returned means the word If is read backwards

parts.note: um is the sound of hesitation
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Tory politician who stops dithering on reflection finds a matter easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple' looks like an adjective but is the old noun for a medicinal plant; 'returned' turns the word If around, and 'without' wraps it round the hesitation sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Fumitory is a herb once used medicinally, and herbs used as medicine were called simples.

clue.text: Having to contend with about fifty, escape!

indicators.note: about means one piece is placed around the other here

parts.note: to contend is to fight
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone facing fifty opponents decides to run for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is an act of running away, a synonym for an escape.

clue.text: Foreign lady compelled to go around after midnight

indicators.note: to go around says the word for compelled encloses the time

parts.note: compelled means made, as in made to do something
am is the abbreviation for the hours after midnight

explanation.surface: A woman from abroad is forced to do rounds in the small hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French title for a married woman, so a lady from abroad.

clue.text: Body found encased in cement-or so the papers say

indicators.note: encased in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tabloid report of a corpse set in concrete, or so the press claims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the papers say' is surface colour around the hidden run in cemenT OR SO; 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A torso is the trunk of the human body without head or limbs.

clue.text: The name of the cleaner taken in free

indicators.note: taken in says the cleaner goes inside the word for free

parts.note: to rid is to free
a char or charwoman is a British word for a cleaning lady

explanation.surface: A cleaner's name is recorded after she is employed for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR, short for charwoman, is a British term for a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard is a common male forename, an example of a name.

clue.text: Dull sovereign's subject

parts.note: matt means dull, without shine
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the monarch

explanation.surface: The topic of a boring monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject' looks like the monarch's subject, a person; it is the definition, a topic.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter is a topic or theme under discussion.

clue.text: Flat-broke tramp with neat appearance

indicators.note: broke signals the letters of the next words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A penniless vagrant who nonetheless looks tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat-broke' reads as one phrase meaning penniless; split it into the definition 'Flat' and the anagram signal 'broke'. 'appearance' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is the British word for a set of rooms on one floor, a synonym.

clue.text: To call in a trainee is the end of the line!

parts.note: to term something is to call or name it
taken as written
taken as written
L is for learner, from the L-plate on a British learner driver's car

explanation.surface: Summoning an apprentice is the last straw.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal is the station at which a railway or bus route finishes.

clue.text: Made up and performed

explanation.surface: Invented and acted.
explanation.definitionFit: To render can mean to make up or cause to become, and also to perform a piece of music or drama.

clue.text: Popular credit arrangement, though far from straightforward

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

indicators.note: arrangement says the letters of credit are rearranged

explanation.surface: A popular loan deal is nonetheless rather devious.
explanation.definitionFit: Indirect means roundabout or devious, the opposite of plain and direct.

clue.text: Soldiers enter a store when wanting fruit

indicators.note: enter says the soldiers go inside the store

parts.note: a barn is a farm building for storing grain
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops go into a shop when they need fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting fruit' means lacking fruit, not desiring it.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren describes a plant or land that produces no crop, lacking offspring.

clue.text: A fellow reading a page after church

indicators.note: after says the following letters come after church

explanation.surface: A man reading a page after the church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is an informal British word for a man, a synonym for fellow.

clue.text: He practises alternative medicine in his house on the ring road

parts.note: his house is his home
a ring is round like the letter O
a path is a way or road

explanation.surface: A herbalist works from home on the ring road.
explanation.definitionFit: Homeopathy is a form of complementary therapy, and its practitioner is a homeopath.

clue.text: A little instant rice is undeniably instant

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bit of quick-cook rice is certainly fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'is undeniably instant' as the definition; only the final 'instant' defines, and 'is undeniably' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In a trice means in an instant, so a trice is a moment.

clue.text: A poet quite the reverse of gloomy

indicators.note: quite the reverse of says the word for gloomy is read backwards

parts.note: drab means dull and gloomy

explanation.surface: A poet who is entirely cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite the reverse of' looks like it means opposite in sense; it means read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a traditional name for a poet, especially Shakespeare.

clue.text: The fans stand here going wild

indicators.note: going wild says the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Supporters in the stand are going crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherents are followers or supporters, the same as fans.

clue.text: Minister making report on parking available

indicators.note: on says the report is placed after the letter for parking

parts.note: P is the sign for parking
to relate is to report or tell

explanation.surface: A clergyman says that a parking space is free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks political but is a church minister. 'making' and 'available' are surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a high-ranking churchman such as a bishop, a minister of religion.

clue.text: A box containing copper? That's right

indicators.note: containing says the box holds the copper

parts.note: a crate is a box
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A box holding a policeman? Correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman; here it is the metal, Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means correct or exact, the same as right.

clue.text: A beastly has-been for clever people to put on

parts.note: MAs are holders of a Master of Arts degree, so learned people
taken as written
to don is to put on clothes

explanation.surface: An old-timer whom brainy people are told to dress up as.
explanation.walkthrough: MAS is the plural of MA, the degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastodon is an extinct elephant-like animal, so a creature that has had its day.

clue.text: Jars for man in form

indicators.note: in says the man sits inside the form

parts.note: a form is a school class
he is a man, the male pronoun

explanation.surface: Jam jars swapped for a man in the school class.
explanation.definitionFit: Jars as a verb means conflicts or grates, as clashes do.

clue.text: Legal suspension of support

explanation.surface: A court order halting a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay of execution is a legal postponement; a stay is also a rope or prop giving support.

clue.text: Pair up and put an end to the game

definitions.text: put an end to the game

explanation.surface: Match together and finish the contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To mate is to couple, and in chess mate is the checkmate that ends play.

clue.text: Men hate ordering fuel

indicators.note: ordering says the letters of the words before it are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Men dislike placing orders for fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is the main component of natural gas, burned for energy.

clue.text: Countenance pocketing one pound is easy

indicators.note: pocketing says the face holds the other letters

parts.note: a countenance is a face
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone's face is easy-going after taking a single pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile means achieved without effort, simple.

clue.text: Like a pipe absorbing the male, it's restorative

indicators.note: absorbing says the word for pipe-like takes in the male

parts.note: reedy describes a thin piping sound like a reed pipe
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A pipe sucking in a man proves healing.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a cure, something that brings back health.

clue.text: Total issue

explanation.surface: Complete output.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter means absolute or complete, and to utter is to say or put out, as in issuing words or coins.

clue.text: Showing unusual talent, are to take turns

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of the following words are made unusual, rearranged

explanation.surface: Talented performers swap places on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To alternate is to do things by turns, one after the other.

clue.text: Hundreds going inside aren't really keen

indicators.note: going inside says the hundreds letter is put within the word aren't

parts.note: the contraction aren't spelt without its apostrophe
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, standing for hundreds

explanation.surface: Hundreds who don't go indoors aren't truly eager.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in aren't is ignored. D is properly 500, used loosely here for hundreds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate and eager.

clue.text: A stimulant in coffee is maybe fine in a restaurant!

indicators.note: in says the rearranged word sits inside the restaurant

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant

indicators.note: maybe says the word fine is only possibly in this form, so rearrange it

explanation.surface: Coffee in a cafe might be fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Caffeine is the alkaloid in coffee and tea that keeps you alert.

clue.text: The guy's a high-flier-a high-minded individual

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle, a bird that soars
St is the abbreviation for saint, a person of high ideals

explanation.surface: This man is a rising star and a principled sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flier' suggests a go-getter; it is the bird. The name also sounds like earnest, adding to the high-minded picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a male forename, so a guy's name.

clue.text: Hardly cut, see!

parts.note: to sever is to cut
Ely is a cathedral city, and a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A clipped exclamation telling someone to look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like the verb; it is a bishop's seat. 'Hardly' means harshly here, not barely.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardly in its old sense means harshly, with severity.
